courseDetails.title: Introduction to Electronic Media
courseDetails.description: A 100-level Mass Communication course introducing radio, television, broadcasting history, production, equipment, terminology, programming, and media laws.

questions.question: Which statement best defines broadcasting?
options: Distribution of content to a dispersed audience through electronic means
questions.explanation: Broadcasting distributes sound, images, or both to many people who may be geographically separated.

questions.question: Which earlier technology provided an important foundation for later electronic communication?
questions.explanation: The telegraph made long-distance electronic communication possible before the telephone and radio developed.

questions.question: Who is associated with the invention of the telephone in 1876?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell made major advances that led to the telephone in 1876.

questions.question: Guglielmo Marconi is important in broadcasting history because he successfully transmitted an early wireless message in
questions.explanation: The course material identifies Marconi’s successful wireless message in 1895 as a landmark in radio communication.

questions.question: Reginald Fessenden’s 1906 achievement mainly improved radio by transmitting
questions.explanation: Fessenden successfully transmitted the human voice, making radio transmission more practical.

questions.question: Lee De Forest’s Audion vacuum tube helped radio broadcasting by making signals
questions.explanation: The Audion vacuum tube improved the clarity and strength of radio signals.

questions.question: Regular colour television transmission began in the period identified in the course material as
questions.explanation: The material states that regular colour transmission began in 1954.

questions.question: The replacement of cathode-ray-tube televisions by LCD displays illustrates the influence of
questions.explanation: Flat-panel LCD displays reflect technological change in television hardware and viewing quality.

questions.question: In the Nigerian broadcasting history presented in the PDF, early radio broadcasting served the colonial government mainly by
options: Keeping people informed about events in the empire
questions.explanation: Early broadcasts relayed information, including news about the British Empire and World War II.

questions.question: The early Nigerian system in which programmes were received and relayed to local audiences was called
questions.explanation: Re-diffusion involved receiving broadcast signals and transmitting them to local audiences.

questions.question: The Nigerian Broadcasting Service was established in
questions.explanation: The NBS was established in 1951 and enabled more local Nigerian broadcasting content.

questions.question: In 1957, the Nigerian Broadcasting Service became the
questions.explanation: The NBS evolved into the Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1957.

questions.question: Western Nigeria Television, established in 1959, was located in
questions.explanation: WNTV was established in Ibadan and is identified in the material as Africa’s first television station.

questions.question: The Nigerian Television Authority was established in
questions.explanation: The NTA was established in 1976 to oversee television broadcasting in Nigeria.

questions.question: The major Nigerian broadcasting change associated with Decree No. 38 of 1992 was
options: The end of all radio broadcasting
Deregulation and permission for private ownership
questions.explanation: Decree No. 38 deregulated broadcasting and broke the government’s monopoly on the airwaves.

questions.question: Which group represents the main structural participants in the broadcast industry?
options: Content creators, networks, distributors, and regulators
questions.explanation: The course describes creators, networks, distribution channels, and regulatory bodies as connected parts of the industry.

questions.question: A production company that creates documentaries is functioning primarily as a
questions.explanation: Content creators produce programmes such as documentaries, news, drama, and live shows.

questions.question: Terrestrial broadcasting normally refers to transmission
questions.explanation: Terrestrial broadcasting uses land-based transmitters to send signals over the air.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of internet broadcasting?
questions.explanation: Internet broadcasting delivers audio or video through online platforms, often on demand.

questions.question: In Nigeria, the body that oversees broadcasting regulation is the
questions.explanation: The National Broadcasting Commission, or NBC, regulates the Nigerian broadcasting sector.

questions.question: A broadcast licence is primarily intended to ensure that a station
options: Operates within legal and regulatory requirements
questions.explanation: Licensing places a station within the legal framework governing broadcast operations.

questions.question: A key economic source of revenue for commercial television is
questions.explanation: Commercial broadcasters commonly earn revenue by selling advertising time.

questions.question: A public-service benefit of broadcasting during a natural disaster is to
options: Provide timely information that can help maintain order
questions.explanation: Broadcasting can quickly distribute warnings, instructions, and verified updates during crises.

questions.question: A content quota requiring a station to transmit a percentage of local programmes is an example of
questions.explanation: Content quotas are regulatory requirements used to support standards or local production.

questions.question: Which situation best illustrates digital disruption in broadcasting?
options: Viewers increasingly use streaming services instead of scheduled television
questions.explanation: Online platforms can change audience habits and create competition for traditional broadcasters.

questions.question: The primary function of a broadcast microphone is to convert
questions.explanation: A microphone captures sound and converts it into an electrical signal for processing or transmission.

questions.question: For a speaker moving around a large outdoor area, the most suitable microphone type from the course list is generally
questions.explanation: An omni-directional microphone picks up sound from all directions and is useful where sound comes from a wide area.

questions.question: A microphone designed to pick up sound mainly from one direction is
questions.explanation: A uni-directional microphone focuses on sound arriving from one direction.

questions.question: Which microphone is small and clipped to a speaker’s clothing?
questions.explanation: A personal microphone is a small clip-on microphone used for individual speakers.

questions.question: A microphone positioned above a performance space to capture a group such as a choir is a
questions.explanation: Hanging microphones are placed above a space to capture sound from a wider area.

questions.question: Which studio light is focused and bright, highlighting the main subject?
questions.explanation: The key light is the focused primary light used to highlight the subject.

questions.question: The main purpose of fill lighting is to
options: Reduce harsh shadows with soft general light
questions.explanation: Fill light provides softer general illumination and helps reduce strong shadows.

questions.question: Back light helps a television subject by
options: Separating the subject from the background
questions.explanation: Light from behind gives the subject separation and helps the subject stand out.

questions.question: The two camera classifications specifically identified in the course are
questions.explanation: The material classifies cameras as monochrome and colour cameras.

questions.question: Compared with monochrome cameras, colour cameras generally require
options: More light to capture images clearly
questions.explanation: The course notes that colour cameras need more light for clear image capture.

questions.question: The main functions of a broadcast console include
questions.explanation: The console manages sound signals by amplifying, mixing, and modulating them.

questions.question: The adjustable controls used on a console to change the level of a sound source are called
questions.explanation: Faders are sliders used to adjust the level of audio sources.

questions.question: A transmitter prepares a broadcast signal by generating, amplifying, and
options: Modulating it before sending it to an antenna
questions.explanation: The transmitter processes the signal and sends it to the antenna for radiation to the audience.

questions.question: In the production chain, the antenna primarily serves to
options: Broadcast the processed signal to the audience
questions.explanation: The antenna radiates the processed radio or television signal to receivers.

questions.question: A low-frequency noise problem caused by alternating current leaking into an audio signal is called
questions.explanation: Hum is unwanted low-frequency noise associated with electrical interference.

questions.question: A sound that bounces off one surface is known as an
questions.explanation: An echo is a reflected sound from one surface; reverberation involves reflections from more than one surface.

questions.question: In radio jargon, to fade a sound means to
questions.explanation: Fade means to gradually reduce the level of music or a microphone.

questions.question: In radio jargon, “roll” means to
options: Bring on a sound or song
questions.explanation: Roll is an instruction to play or bring in a sound element such as a song or effect.

questions.question: The red On-Air light indicates that
questions.explanation: The On-Air indicator warns people that live microphones are open and background noise must be avoided.

questions.question: In radio scheduling, the 24-hour clock represents 1:00 p.m. as
questions.explanation: 1:00 p.m. is 13:00 in the 24-hour clock.

questions.question: The three broad stages of radio production are
questions.explanation: Radio production begins with planning, moves to recording or live transmission, and ends with post-production where required.

questions.question: Which activity belongs primarily to radio pre-production?
questions.explanation: Pre-production involves planning the programme, selecting topics, writing scripts, and arranging guests and resources.

questions.question: The stage in which actual recording or live transmission takes place is
questions.explanation: Production is the execution stage where the programme is recorded or transmitted live.

questions.question: Editing recorded radio content is part of
questions.explanation: Post-production polishes recorded content by editing, adding effects, and adjusting audio quality.

questions.question: Which radio-production element can create suspense through a deliberate pause?
questions.explanation: Strategic silence can create suspense, signal transitions, or give listeners time to reflect.

questions.question: In radio storytelling, sound effects are especially important because they
options: Create vivid images in listeners’ minds
questions.explanation: Listeners cannot see the scene, so sound effects help them imagine places, actions, and transitions.

questions.question: Who is primarily responsible for overseeing a radio programme from pre-production through post-production?
questions.explanation: The producer coordinates the complete production process and ensures that objectives and deadlines are met.

questions.question: The radio team member who guides the show, introduces segments, and interviews guests is the
questions.explanation: The presenter is the on-air voice who connects the programme’s segments and audience.

questions.question: The person responsible for setting microphones, controlling levels, and mixing sound is the
questions.explanation: The sound engineer handles the technical quality and balance of audio.

questions.question: The radio scriptwriter’s main responsibility is to
options: Develop programme content and structure dialogue or questions
questions.explanation: The scriptwriter creates content, dialogue, interview questions, and the programme’s flow.

questions.question: A key challenge of a live radio programme is that
options: All errors can be corrected after transmission
Strict timing and coordination are required
questions.explanation: Live broadcasting occurs in real time, so timing and coordination are essential because mistakes cannot simply be edited out.

questions.question: A radio script should use short, clear sentences mainly because
options: Listeners may need to understand the message on the first hearing
questions.explanation: Radio listeners cannot inspect a page while listening, so clarity on first hearing is important.

questions.question: The five Ws used to make a radio message complete are who, what, when, where, and
questions.explanation: The five Ws are Who, What, When, Where, and Why; some programmes may also require How.

questions.question: A conversational tone in radio writing is intended to
options: Make listeners feel personally addressed and connected
questions.explanation: Writing as if speaking to one listener makes the broadcast more natural and engaging.

questions.question: Recency in radio scriptwriting means that the content should be
questions.explanation: Recency keeps news and other programme content relevant to present circumstances.

questions.question: The correct order of the three main television production stages in the course is
questions.explanation: Planning comes first, filming or recording follows, and editing and finishing come afterward.

questions.question: A storyboard is best described as
options: A visual sequence showing how scenes will appear
questions.explanation: Storyboards visually represent the script and help plan the sequence and appearance of scenes.

questions.question: Location scouting is undertaken mainly to
options: Find a suitable and accessible place for filming
questions.explanation: The production team checks whether a location fits the script and can accommodate the crew and equipment.

questions.question: Budgeting and scheduling are normally completed during
questions.explanation: Budgeting and scheduling prepare the project financially and temporally before filming begins.

questions.question: During television production, the director is chiefly responsible for
options: The overall creative vision and directing the crew
questions.explanation: The director makes creative decisions and guides actors and crew so the production achieves its vision.

questions.question: Which television production role normally manages logistics, budget, and scheduling?
questions.explanation: The producer oversees the project from start to finish and manages its practical resources.

questions.question: The set designer creates
options: The visual environment in which the programme takes place
questions.explanation: Set designers build or arrange scenery that matches the script’s visual requirements.

questions.question: In post-production, colour grading adjusts the footage’s
questions.explanation: Colour grading refines the visual appearance by adjusting colour, contrast, and brightness.

questions.question: Non-linear editing software is useful because it allows editors to
options: Experiment with different programme versions efficiently
questions.explanation: Digital non-linear editing makes it easier to rearrange and test footage during post-production.

questions.question: Virtual sets commonly combine green-screen technology with
questions.explanation: Virtual sets use green screens and computer-generated backgrounds to create realistic environments.

questions.question: In television production, “talent” refers to
options: People who appear on camera, such as presenters or actors
questions.explanation: Talent includes on-camera presenters, actors, news anchors, and similar performers.

questions.question: The rehearse-record method involves
options: Editing only after a live broadcast
Rehearsing scenes and recording them in segments
questions.explanation: Scenes are rehearsed first and then recorded segment by segment, allowing detailed preparation.

questions.question: Which production method transmits a programme in real time?
questions.explanation: Live broadcasting sends the programme to the audience as it happens.

questions.question: Basic retakes are useful because they allow a production team to
options: Stop recording and correct an error by re-shooting a scene
Transmit from any location without equipment
Remove the need for a director
questions.explanation: Basic retakes provide a chance to correct mistakes without re-shooting the entire programme.

questions.question: A close-up shot is particularly effective for
options: Showing the entire country at once
Directing attention to a character’s facial expression
questions.explanation: A close-up limits the visual field and highlights details such as facial expression.

questions.question: In television, program control is the area where the director
options: Selects and organises the audio and visual elements
questions.explanation: Program control is the centre for managing what the audience sees and hears during production.

questions.question: Switching in television production means
options: Choosing and arranging video images from different sources
Changing a script from English to French
questions.explanation: A switcher selects which camera or video source is sent to air at a given moment.

questions.question: The character generator is used to create and manage
options: On-screen text such as titles and credits
questions.explanation: A character generator produces text graphics displayed over television pictures.

questions.question: The audio control booth is responsible for
options: Managing microphones, mixers, and television sound
questions.explanation: Audio control manages the sound sources and keeps audio levels balanced with the picture.

questions.question: Master control in a television station functions as the hub that
options: Schedules and transmits programme inputs at the correct time
questions.explanation: Master control handles programme inputs, commercials, and live transmissions and ensures correct timing and standards.

questions.question: In television jargon, 1080i is associated with
questions.explanation: The course lists 720p and 1080i as higher-quality HDTV resolutions.

questions.question: RGB in television imaging stands for
questions.explanation: Red, green, and blue are the primary component colours used to create images on screen.

questions.question: Streaming differs from downloading because streaming allows a user to
options: Watch or listen while data is still being delivered
Edit every file before opening it
questions.explanation: Streaming delivers a continuous flow that can be consumed while delivery is in progress.

questions.question: In television terminology, a field is
questions.explanation: The course defines a field as a location outside the regular studio.

questions.question: If a presenter is reading narration over accompanying pictures, the technique is called
questions.explanation: Voice-over is narration delivered over visuals or other programme material.

questions.question: A programme proposal is primarily used to present the producer’s plan, including the objective, format, and
questions.explanation: The course identifies the objective, show format, and tentative budget as typical proposal elements.

questions.question: The first creative step in developing a television programme is usually
questions.explanation: Programme ideation generates and refines the concept that becomes the basis of production.

questions.question: A producer watching a shoot to ensure that the overall look and flow still match the concept is performing
questions.explanation: The producer observes the production and provides feedback so the work remains aligned with its original purpose.

questions.question: A television scriptwriter should conduct research primarily to
options: Present accurate information and strengthen credibility
questions.explanation: Research gives the writer accurate knowledge and helps produce credible, engaging content.

questions.question: Following a station’s script layout is important because it
options: Guarantees that every programme is live
Maintains consistency with the station’s house style
questions.explanation: Each station may have preferred formatting and style conventions that writers are expected to follow.

questions.question: Originality in television scriptwriting requires a writer to
options: Develop authentic content rather than copy another script
questions.explanation: Original, authentic work is both ethically sound and more likely to reflect the intended audience and environment.

questions.question: Why should a television scriptwriter pay attention to audience perspective?
options: It removes the need for a format
Television viewers often have limited attention spans
questions.explanation: Concise, engaging scenes help retain television viewers whose attention may be shorter than that of readers.

questions.question: Outside broadcasting is the transmission of a programme
options: From a location outside the regular studio
questions.explanation: Outside broadcasting uses a mobile production setup to cover events or programmes away from the studio.

questions.question: An OB unit is best described as
options: A mobile production unit with equipment and crew
questions.explanation: An outside-broadcast unit carries the equipment and personnel needed to produce from the field.

questions.question: Electronic News Gathering is especially associated with
options: Collecting audio and video news material in the field
questions.explanation: ENG is a field-gathering approach used for news and other location-based coverage.

questions.question: A studio manager’s important live-broadcast responsibility is to
options: Decide the meaning of every news story
Help ensure equipment and technical operations work smoothly
questions.explanation: Studio managers support the technical and operational side of productions and respond to problems quickly.

questions.question: The National Broadcasting Commission in Nigeria was created by
questions.explanation: The course and the NBC Act identify Decree No. 38 of 1992 as the establishing instrument for the Commission.

questions.question: Defamation law mainly protects a person’s
options: Reputation from false and damaging statements
questions.explanation: Defamation concerns false statements that harm reputation, so broadcasters must verify damaging allegations carefully.

questions.question: When reporting a sensitive allegation, the most responsible first step is to
options: Verify the facts and avoid presenting an unproven claim as established truth
questions.explanation: Accuracy, verification, fairness, and careful language reduce the risk of unethical or unlawful reporting.

questions.question: The central legal and ethical challenge in broadcasting is to balance freedom of expression with
options: Accountability and the protection of people and society
questions.explanation: Media laws seek to protect expression while requiring broadcasters to operate responsibly and within legal limits.
